messages:
sam.nguyen: Heads-up — I'm seeing a spike in p95 latency on the KV read path for /search prefixes. Dashboard shows overall traffic fine but the prefix cache hit-rate looks like it dropped. Can someone point me to the panel that breaks hit-rate by prefix? Also wondering if we have a prefix-level alert tuned (it's noisy if it exists).

anya: Grafana has the dashboard — KV -> Cache -> Prefix hit rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv-prefix-cache?var-env=prod . Panel name is 'prefix_hitrate (by prefix)'. If you're on Datadog the metric is `redwood.kv.prefix_cache.hit_rate` with a `prefix` tag.

micah: FWIW the panel uses a Prometheus-style query (we proxy metrics): `sum by(prefix) (rate(kv_prefix_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(prefix) (rate(kv_prefix_cache_requests_total[5m]))`. We also emit per-route breadcrumbs in logs at /observability/kv_prefix.log if you need raw evidence.

obs-bot: ALERT: kv-prefix-hitrate-low fired for prefix=/search on prod at 2025-05-10T12:34:18Z — threshold 0.6 over 5m.

dave.b: That monitor has been noisy during rollout windows and cold restarts. Proposal: change to a 15m evaluation window and require both low hit-rate and elevated p95 latency before alerting. Something like: alert when `hit_rate < 0.5` for >10m AND `p95_latency > 250ms`. Also group alerts by `prefix` so we don't get a flood for low-traffic prefixes.

irene: I opened a small PR to adjust the Datadog monitor + add a suppression rule for autoscaler restarts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-monitoring/pull/482 — includes suggested query and a mute-on-label `k8s.autoscaler=true`. Code snippet from the PR: 
```
avg(last_15m): (sum:redwood.kv.prefix_cache.hit_rate{env:prod}.rollup(avg, 60)) by {prefix} < 0.5
```
and we add a suppression window keyed off `k8s.autoscaler` events.

sam.nguyen: Perfect, thanks. I'll watch the PR and add a short runbook note in the incident playbook. One more ask: where do I find traces that link a cache miss to the origin read? Need to pull trace ids for the client repro.

anya: Traces live in Jaeger: https://jaeger.redwood.local/search — use operation `kv.read` and filter span tag `cache_hit=false`. There's a saved query called 'kv-miss->origin' on the observability team dashboard.

micah: If you want raw logs you can use LogQL: `{service="kv", prefix="/search"} |= "cache_miss" | json` — then join on the `trace_id` field to pull the distributed trace.

sam.nguyen: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short follow-up with the affected client id and link to the PR. @irene @dave.b can you review quickly? :thumbsup:
